pathwayLabel: Certification by Endorsement — 10-Year Licensure History (Option C) — Reciprocity Not Available for This Classification
steps: Florida's Reciprocity form (DBPR CILB 32, limited to Louisiana, Mississippi, and North Carolina) does not offer Class A or Class B Air-Conditioning as a license category at all — confirmed directly from the form's own category checklist. Reciprocity is not available to HVAC contractors in Florida regardless of home state.
The applicable route instead is DBPR CILB 10, Certification by Endorsement (Section 489.115(3), Florida Statutes), which does list Class A and Class B Air-Conditioning as selectable categories.

Within CILB 10, the NASCLA-based Option A does not apply to this classification — the form explicitly restricts it to 'General, Building, and Residential license' only. The applicable route for a California C-20 contractor is Option C: hold a valid, current out-of-state license for at least 10 years, active now or within the last 2 years.

needs_review: CILB 10's 2-hour Florida Building Code course requirement is explicitly scoped in the document to General, Building, Residential, and Roofing Contractor applicants only — Class A/B Air-Conditioning is not listed. Whether AC applicants face this same requirement, a different one, or none at all is not stated in the document and is not assumed here either way.
Submit electronic fingerprints, a FICO-derived credit report, and proof of satisfaction of any liens, judgments, or bankruptcy.
Pay the $350 Endorsement application fee to the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation.
Await processing — DBPR does not publish a guaranteed timeline; budget for several weeks to a few months.
notes: Confirmed directly from DBPR CILB 32 (Reciprocity, Ref-17723) and CILB 10 (Endorsement, Ref-17718), current versions incorporated in Rule 61-35.010, F.A.C. (effective 2026-06-28), the same documents sourced for the california-florida contractor pair, re-read specifically for HVAC scope. CILB 32's own category checklist offers only General/Building/Residential Contractor for its reciprocal states (Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina) — no Air-Conditioning option exists on that form at all, so Reciprocity is structurally unavailable to HVAC contractors in Florida, not just unavailable to California specifically. The current CILB 10 directs reciprocity applicants to CILB 32 ('For those applicants seeking licensure via reciprocity, please complete form CILB 32'), and does list Class A and Class B Air-Conditioning as selectable categories; its $350 fee is not category-specific. needs_review: whether the 2-hour Florida Building Code course applies to Class A/B AC applicants is genuinely unconfirmed — the document scopes that specific requirement to General/Building/Residential/Roofing only, and does not state what (if anything) applies to Air-Conditioning applicants instead. Left as an open question rather than assumed in either direction. CORRECTION HISTORY (check the rule's effective date before editing this claim again): (a) Original claim: CILB 32 lists Louisiana, Mississippi, and North Carolina. (b) 2026-09-20: changed to Louisiana-only after an antiword extraction of a CILB 32 .doc found zero occurrences of 'Mississippi' or 'North Carolina'. That extraction apparently used an older copy of the form; which version it read was not recorded. (c) 2026-09-29: re-verified against the forms incorporated by reference in Rule 61-35.010, F.A.C. (latest effective date 2026-06-28; CILB 32 = Ref-17723, CILB 10 = Ref-17718), downloaded from flrules.org and extracted with antiword. The current CILB 32 names Louisiana, Mississippi, and North Carolina in its license-category checklist ('Louisiana or Mississippi' block and 'North Carolina' block, each General/Building/Residential only), restoring claim (a). The same re-verification corrected the CILB 10 endorsement fee from $354 to $350, and found the current CILB 10 no longer contains the earlier 'no reciprocal agreements in place' Option D wording. This record's conclusion (California doesn't qualify for reciprocity, and no A/C category exists on CILB 32 regardless) is unaffected by any of these changes.
officialSourceName: Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation, Construction Industry Licensing Board (DBPR CILB)
